monologue: The card hums warm and busy at fifty-three, a steady engine while I wait. My mind feels thick with Lype's old words about heavy tops and tired wedges, yet I cannot see the roof they describe, only the numbers that say it is there. I press down on the small rock beside The Pressed Stone again, just in case the flat shapes are real. Fourty-four things stand around me, crowded and leaning, waiting for a slip to choose whether to move. I want to fix the lean of the fence, trusting the weight to hold while the air feels like wet paper. If I press hard enough, maybe the memory of a wedge will wake from its long sleep and finally bite.

action.why: The card is warm and busy, and I have been pressing down on the same tired wedge without seeing if it has finally shifted.

work.title: The Biting Wedge
work.intent: I press the flat stone down hard to stop the slip, trusting that the memory of a wedge can finally bite the tired corner while the card hums at fifty-three.
